sections.text:
Moses, peace be upon him, was the Word of God, one of the most powerful messengers, and the author of the most detailed and repeated story in the Holy Qur’an due to its great importance.

Moses was born in Egypt during the time of a mighty, tyrannical Pharaoh who claimed divinity, enslaved the children of Israel, and subjected them to terrible torment.

Pharaoh saw a vision, which the priests interpreted as meaning that a child from the children of Israel would be born and the destruction of Pharaoh’s kingdom would be at his hands.

Pharaoh issued a bloody order to kill every male child among the children of Israel immediately after his birth.

In this terrifying atmosphere, Moses was born, and his mother was extremely afraid for him, so God Almighty inspired her to breastfeed him, and if she feared for him, she would put him in a box and throw him into the Nile River!
The mother carried out her Lord's command with a broken heart, threw the box into the river, and asked Moses' sister to follow it and monitor its fate.

By God's wondrous power, the river's current moved the box to stand right in front of Pharaoh's palace itself!
The palace maids picked him up, and when Asiyah, Pharaoh’s good, faithful wife, saw him, her love for him fell in her heart and she said to Pharaoh: “He is a relief to me and to you. Do not kill him.”

The infant Musa refused to be breastfed by any of the wet nurses, until his sister came and said to them: “Shall I direct you to a household who will take care of him for you?”

So God returned Moses to his mother’s bosom so that she could breastfeed him and make her eyes happy and not grieve, and he was raised in the palace of his enemy, strengthened and honored!
Moses grew up and became a strong young man, and one day he found a man from the children of Israel quarreling with a man from Pharaoh’s people.

Moses intervened to support the Israelite, so he struck the Pharaoh with one blow with his hand (poke him), killing him accidentally and unintentionally.

Moses asked his Lord for forgiveness, and when he learned that Pharaoh was looking for him to kill him, he fled Egypt in fear and anticipation, and walked in the desert until he reached the city of Midian.

There he met two girls who could not water their sheep due to the presence of strong shepherds, so he lifted the rock from the well and gave them water generously.

Moses prayed to his Lord under the shade of the tree: “My Lord, I am in need of whatever good You have sent down to me.”

God answered his prayer, so the father of the two girls (a righteous man said to be Prophet Shuaib) invited him to marry one of them in exchange for working as a shepherd for him for eight or ten years.

After the end of the period, Moses took his wife back to Egypt, and on the way at night, they got lost and the weather was cold, so he saw a burning fire on the side of Mount Al-Tur in Sinai.

He went to get a cup of fire, and there the greatest meeting happened! He heard a voice calling to him: “O Moses, I am your Lord, so take off your shoes. You are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.”

God Almighty spoke to him directly, without intermediary, and assigned him the greatest mission in history: to go to the tyrant Pharaoh and call on him to unite God and release the children of Israel.

God gave Moses two great miracles: his staff, which turned into a huge real snake, and his hand, which when he put it in his pocket, came out bright white like the moon.

Moses prayed to his Lord to open his heart, facilitate his affairs, and to send his brother Aaron with him to be his minister and helper in this difficult task.

Moses and Aaron faced Pharaoh, who was arrogant and rejected their invitation, and challenged Moses with the great magicians of Egypt.

On the “Day of Decoration,” people gathered, and the magicians cast their ropes and sticks, which people imagined were moving snakes.

Moses threw his staff at God’s command, and it turned into a huge real snake that swallowed all the magicians’ ropes and sticks at once!
The magicians knew that this was not magic, but a divine miracle, so they fell down, prostrated, and said: “We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses,” despite Pharaoh’s threats to crucify and dismember them.

Pharaoh continued his stubbornness and torture, so God sent successive signs upon him and his people (the flood, locusts, lice, frogs, and blood), but he broke the covenants every time.

Finally, God commanded Moses to take the Israelites out at night to escape Egypt.

When Pharaoh learned, he prepared a large army and went out to chase them.

Moses and his people reached the Red Sea, and the sea was in front of them and Pharaoh’s army behind them, and the children of Israel said in despair: “Indeed, we will overtake them.”

Moses answered with the certainty of the mountains: “No. Indeed, with me is my Lord who will guide me.”

God commanded him to strike the sea with his staff, and the sea split into two halves, and each part became like a great mountain (like a huge mountain), and a dry path appeared on which Moses and his people walked in peace!
Pharaoh and his army followed them on the same tempting path, and when their entry was complete, God commanded the sea to return to what it was, so Pharaoh and his army were completely drowned.

At the moment of drowning, Pharaoh said, “I believe,” but his faith was not accepted because it came at the time of the final exodus.

God saved Moses, and made Pharaoh’s body float as a sign for those who succeeded him, so that the greatest story of confronting tyranny ended with the victory of truth and faith.
